summary_zh: 學會帶新同事熟悉環境時的實用說法，並分清楚 stop／remember／try 後面接 V-ing 和 to V 意思不一樣。大約 15 分鐘可以做完，口說用安靜模式打字也算。

vocab.example: Priya will help you learn the ropes during your first week.

vocab.example: Our billing system has a steep learning curve, so don't worry if it feels slow at first.
vocab.example_zh: 我們的請款系統很難上手，所以一開始覺得慢也別擔心。

vocab.definition: to learn how to do something after some practice
vocab.example: It took me a month to get the hang of the reporting tool.
vocab.example_zh: 我花了一個月才抓到那個報表工具的訣竅。

vocab.definition: to follow an experienced person at work and watch what they do so you can learn
vocab.example: On Wednesday, you'll shadow Ken on his client calls.
vocab.example_zh: 星期三你會跟著 Ken，在旁邊觀摩他打給客戶的電話。

vocab.definition: all the small details of how something works
vocab.example: Nobody knows the ins and outs of our expense policy better than Lisa.
vocab.example_zh: 沒有人比 Lisa 更清楚我們報帳規定的眉角。

vocab.zh: 入職夥伴（帶新人的同事）
vocab.definition: a coworker who is chosen to help a new employee with everyday questions
vocab.example: If you're not sure who to ask, start with your onboarding buddy. That's the teammate assigned to help you settle in.
vocab.example_zh: 如果不確定該問誰，就先問你的入職夥伴，那是公司指派來幫你適應環境的同事。

vocab.definition: a diagram that shows who works in which team and who reports to whom
vocab.example: I printed the org chart so I could see who reports to whom.
vocab.example_zh: 我把組織圖印出來，才看得出誰向誰報告。

vocab.definition: special words used by a group of people that others find hard to understand
vocab.example: Stop me if I use too much jargon. We have an acronym for everything here.
vocab.example_zh: 如果我講太多行話就打斷我。我們這裡什麼都有縮寫。

reading.title: Helping a New Teammate Settle In
paragraphs: Most people remember starting a new job: the new badge, the unfamiliar faces, the long list of passwords. For someone joining your team, the first two weeks can decide whether they feel welcome or lost. Here is how our team tries to make that time easier.

First, every new hire gets an onboarding buddy. The buddy is not their manager. Their job is to answer the small questions people are too shy to ask, like where to find the first-aid kit and some over-the-counter painkillers, or how many vacation days carry over to next year. On day one, the buddy takes the new person to lunch with a few teammates. It is an easy way to break the ice.

Second, we plan for the learning curve. Nobody can learn the ins and outs of our systems in a week, so we give new teammates one tool at a time. They shadow a colleague on real calls before they handle their own. We also share the org chart, which shows at a glance who works on what.
Third, we cut the jargon. When a new teammate looks confused, we stop to explain the acronym instead of hurrying on. Our newest engineer said this helped her more than any manual.

Finally, we check in often. A new hire who has come down with a cold, or whose back pain has flared up, should not feel they have to prove themselves by working through it. Most people get the hang of things within a month. Our job is to make sure they don't feel run-down along the way.

questions.q: According to the article, what is the onboarding buddy's main job?
options: To review the new hire's work every week
To answer everyday questions the new hire may be too shy to ask
To write the training manual for new hires
To decide which tools the new hire uses first
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：Their job is to answer the small questions people are too shy to ask. 文章也特別說 The buddy is not their manager，所以不是審核工作的人。

questions.q: Why do new teammates shadow a colleague first?
options: Because the team has too few clients
Because they need to learn the systems step by step before handling calls alone
Because the manager is too busy to train them
Because the org chart is out of date
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：Nobody can learn the ins and outs of our systems in a week… They shadow a colleague on real calls before they handle their own. 一步一步來，先觀摩再自己上場。

questions.q: What can we infer about the team from the last paragraph?
options: It expects new hires to work late to prove themselves.
It cares about new hires' health, not just their speed.
It gives new hires extra sick days.
It thinks most new hires leave within a month.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：最後一段說生病或背痛發作的新人 should not feel they have to prove themselves by working through it，還要確保他們不會 run-down，可推論這個團隊在意新人的身體，不只是上手快不快。文中沒提到額外病假。

grammar.point: Gerund vs infinitive: stop doing / stop to do, remember, try
grammar.point_zh: 動名詞 vs 不定詞：stop／remember／try 後面接 V-ing 或 to V，意思不一樣

guide.key_zh: stop／remember：V-ing＝在做或做過，to V＝接著要做。try：V-ing＝試方法，to V＝努力做到。

uses.label_zh: stop：停掉正在做的事 vs 停下來去做另一件事
uses.note_zh: stop to V 的 to＝為了去做

uses.label_zh: remember：記得做過 vs 記得要去做
uses.note_zh: V-ing＝過去的回憶；to V＝還沒做、別忘了

uses.label_zh: try：試試看某個方法 vs 努力想做到
uses.note_zh: try V-ing＝實驗看看有沒有效；try to V＝想辦法完成（不容易）

mistakes.wrong: Remember locking the door when you leave tonight.
mistakes.right: Remember to lock the door when you leave tonight.
mistakes.why_zh: tonight 還沒發生，是提醒要去做的事 → remember to V

mistakes.wrong: I stopped to check my phone during meetings because it was rude.
mistakes.right: I stopped checking my phone during meetings because it was rude.
mistakes.why_zh: 因為覺得沒禮貌，所以「戒掉、不再做」這個習慣 → stop V-ing；stop to check 是「停下來去看手機」，和 because it was rude 的邏輯不合

examples.en: On the way in, I stopped to buy coffee for the new hire.
examples.zh: 進公司的路上，我停下來幫新同事買咖啡。

examples.en: I still remember meeting my first manager. Please remember to send Hana the welcome email.
examples.zh: 我還記得和我的第一個主管見面的情景。請記得寄歡迎信給 Hana。

examples.en: The VPN wouldn't connect, so I tried restarting my laptop, and it worked.
examples.zh: VPN 一直連不上，所以我試著重開筆電，結果就好了。

exercises.q: Please remember ___ (sign) the visitor log before you leave the building today.
exercises.explain_zh: today 還沒做完，是提醒對方「別忘了要去簽」→ remember to V：to sign。

exercises.q: I remember ___ (meet) Priya at the job fair last year. She asked really good questions.
exercises.explain_zh: last year 是已經發生的事，「記得做過」→ remember V-ing：meeting。

exercises.q: The printer kept jamming, so I tried ___ (use) a different paper tray, and it worked.
exercises.explain_zh: 換紙匣是「試一個方法看看有沒有效」，後面的 and it worked 就是實驗的結果 → try V-ing：using。

exercises.q: I'm trying ___ (finish) the security training before Friday, but the videos keep freezing.
exercises.explain_zh: 目標是「把訓練做完」，一直努力但遇到困難（影片一直卡住）→ try to V：to finish。

exercises.q: Halfway through the office tour, Sam stopped ___ the new hire to the head of IT.
options: to introduce
introducing
introduce
introduced
exercises.explain_zh: Sam 是在導覽途中停下來，「為了去介紹」新人 → stop to V：stopped to introduce。stopped introducing 會變成「不再介紹」，和導覽的情境不合。

exercises.q: You can stop ___ every time you ask a question. Everyone was new once.
options: to apologize
apologize
apologizing
apologized
exercises.explain_zh: 意思是「不要再一直道歉了」，停掉正在做的習慣 → stop V-ing：stop apologizing。stop to apologize 是「停下來去道歉」，意思完全不同。

review.point: Indirect questions: Could you tell me where…
review.point_zh: 間接問句：Could you tell me where…（禮貌地問問題）

exercises.q: [Where is the IT help desk?] → Could you tell me ___?
exercises.answer: where the IT help desk is
exercises.explain_zh: 放進 Could you tell me 後面要改成直述句順序：主詞 the IT help desk 在前，is 移到最後。

exercises.q: [When does the security training start?] → Do you know ___?
exercises.explain_zh: 間接問句拿掉 does，動詞自己變化：主詞 the security training 是單數，所以 start 加 s → when the security training starts。
accept: when the security training will start

exercises.q: [Can I bring my own laptop?] → I was wondering ___.
exercises.answer: if I can bring my own laptop
accept: whether I can bring my own laptop
if I could bring my own laptop
whether I could bring my own laptop
exercises.explain_zh: 原本是 yes/no 問題，沒有疑問詞，要補 if 或 whether，再接直述句順序 I can bring。I was wondering 後面也常把 can 改成 could，更客氣。

guide.key_zh: Could you tell me／Do you know 後面改用「主詞＋動詞」順序，不加 do／does／did。

uses.label_zh: 問 wh- 問題（哪裡、什麼時候、多久…）
uses.form: Could you tell me + where / when / how long + S + V
uses.signal: Could you tell me / Do you know
uses.note_zh: where is it → where it is

uses.label_zh: 問「是不是／有沒有」（yes/no 問題）
uses.form: Do you know + if / whether + S + V
uses.note_zh: 原本沒有疑問詞，就補 if 或 whether

uses.label_zh: 用直述句帶出問題，更委婉
uses.form: I was wondering + if / wh- + S + V
uses.signal: I was wondering / I'd like to know

mistakes.wrong: Could you tell me where is the returns desk?
mistakes.right: Could you tell me where the returns desk is?
mistakes.why_zh: 間接問句裡要用直述句順序：主詞 the returns desk 放在 is 前面

mistakes.wrong: Do you know when does the store close?
mistakes.right: Do you know when the store closes?
mistakes.why_zh: 不加 does，動詞直接變化：the store closes

mistakes.wrong: Can you tell me do you have this in black?
mistakes.right: Can you tell me if you have this in black?
mistakes.why_zh: yes/no 問題要用 if 或 whether 接起來

writing.task: You started a new job three days ago. Write a short message to your onboarding buddy in three short parts: (1) what you've done so far, (2) one thing you're trying to do but finding hard, and (3) two polite questions. Don't join two complete sentences with only a comma.
writing.task_zh: 你到新公司上班第三天。寫一則短訊息給你的入職夥伴，分三小段：(1) 到目前為止做了什麼；(2) 一件你正在努力但覺得很難的事；(3) 兩個禮貌的問題。不要只用逗號把兩個完整的句子接在一起。
writing.sample:
Hi Priya,

Thanks for all your help this week. So far, I've set up my laptop and finished two of the training videos. I've also met most of the people on the org chart.

I'm trying to learn the reporting tool, but it has a steep learning curve. I keep forgetting which filter to use. I think I'll get the hang of it after a few more days.

Could you tell me when we usually send the weekly report? I was also wondering if I could shadow you when you prepare it on Thursday.

Thanks,
Hana
checklist_zh: 有沒有分成三小段：做了什麼、正在努力的事、兩個問題
so far 後面用現在完成式（I've set up、I've finished）
I'm trying to 後面接原形動詞（try to V＝努力想做到）
間接問句用直述句順序：Could you tell me when we usually send…（不是 when do we send）
沒有只用逗號把兩個完整的句子接在一起

reading.title: Why So Many New Hires Quietly Check Out
paragraphs: Companies spend a small fortune finding the right person, then often leave that person to fend for themselves the moment they walk through the door. A laptop, a stack of policies and a cheerful "Let us know if you need anything" is still, in many offices, all that passes for onboarding. It is hardly surprising that a sizable share of new employees start looking around again within their first six months.

The problem is rarely a lack of goodwill. Managers are swamped, and they assume that a capable hire will pick things up as they go. But capable people are also the ones least likely to admit they are struggling. They nod along in meetings full of acronyms, quietly google the jargon afterward and spend their evenings trying to reverse-engineer how things are actually done. By the time anyone notices, the new hire has often concluded that the job isn't what they signed up for.

Teams that get onboarding right tend to do a few unglamorous things consistently. They break the work into stages, so a new person isn't drinking from a fire hose in week one. They pair the newcomer with a buddy who is not their boss, which takes the sting out of asking basic questions. And they schedule short check-ins rather than waiting for a formal review, because problems that are spotted early are usually cheap to fix.

None of this requires a bigger budget. What it requires is someone deciding that the first ninety days are part of the job, not a prelude to it. The payoff is a teammate who feels settled in rather than tolerated, and who is far more likely to still be around a year later.

questions.q: According to the writer, why do capable new hires often struggle unnoticed?
options: They are given too little work to do.
They rarely admit that they need help.
Their managers refuse to answer questions.
They are not interested in the company's goals.
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：capable people are also the ones least likely to admit they are struggling. 能幹的人最不會承認自己有困難，所以別人看不出來。

questions.q: What does the writer imply about the phrase "Let us know if you need anything"?
options: It is the most effective way to welcome a new hire.
It sounds friendly but is not real support.
It should only be said by a buddy, not a manager.
It is required by most company policies.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：第一段說這句話加上一台筆電和一疊規定 is still… all that passes for onboarding，passes for 暗示「被當成」入職訓練、其實不夠格。聽起來友善，但不是真正的支援。

questions.q: Why does the writer recommend short, regular check-ins?
options: Because formal reviews are not allowed in the first year
Because new hires prefer not to talk to their managers
Because problems found early are easier and cheaper to solve
Because buddies are usually too busy to help
questions.explain_zh: 第三段說 problems that are spotted early are usually cheap to fix，所以不要等正式考核，定期短暫關心比較能及早發現、處理問題。

listening.title: The Buddy Who Was Never Around

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Olivia
lines.text: Hey, got a minute? It's about Daniel, the new analyst.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ryan
lines.text: Sure. Is he settling in OK? I've been meaning to check in with him, but this week's been—

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Olivia
lines.text: Crazy, I know. That's kind of the issue. He mentioned he hasn't really seen his buddy since day one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ryan
lines.text: Wait, his buddy is Sophie, right? She's been working flat out on the audit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Olivia
lines.text: Exactly. So he's been trying to figure out the reporting tool on his own, and, well, he sent the wrong numbers to finance yesterday.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ryan
lines.text: Oh no. Was it a big deal?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Olivia
lines.text: Not huge. I caught it before it went any further. But he looked mortified. I think he thinks we're judging him.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ryan
lines.text: Right. Okay, that's on us, not him. What if we swap his buddy? Ken's got more breathing room this month.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Olivia
lines.text: That'd help. And maybe you could stop by his desk today, just to say the mistake's no big deal?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ryan
lines.text: Will do. I'll grab him for a coffee after lunch. Remind me to tell Sophie first, though. I don't want her to hear it secondhand.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Olivia
lines.text: Good call. She'll probably be relieved, honestly.

questions.q: Why did Daniel send the wrong numbers to finance?
options: He didn't care about the report.
He was learning the reporting tool without any help.
Sophie gave him the wrong file.
Finance changed the deadline.
questions.explain_zh: Olivia 說他的入職夥伴 Sophie 忙著稽核，所以 he's been trying to figure out the reporting tool on his own，才會傳錯數字。

questions.q: What does Ryan mean when he says "that's on us, not him"?
options: Daniel should apologize to the team.
The team is responsible because Daniel wasn't supported.
Ryan will fix the numbers himself.
Finance made the real mistake.
questions.explain_zh: 推論題：that's on us＝是我們的責任。Ryan 的意思是新人沒有得到協助，錯在團隊，不在 Daniel。

questions.q: Why does Ryan want to talk to Sophie first?
options: He needs her permission to change the report.
He doesn't want her to find out about the change from someone else.
He wants her to apologize to Daniel.
He thinks she should stay Daniel's buddy.
questions.explain_zh: Ryan 說 I don't want her to hear it secondhand. secondhand＝從別人那裡間接聽到。他想親自告訴 Sophie 換夥伴的事。

dictation: He mentioned he hasn't really seen his buddy since day one.
